topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course structure, her background, and the primary learning outcomes regarding environmental carcinogens and cancer development.

topics.label: Cancer etiology, predisposition, and epidemiological variation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the conceptual foundations of cancer development by examining the interplay between genetic mutations, endogenous processes, environmental exposures, and population-level incidence patterns.

topics.label: Pathogen-driven carcinogenesis and Burkitt lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents promote malignant transformation, using the multi-factorial etiology of Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed case study.

topics.label: Mutagenic DNA damage and metabolic activation of carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how physical, dietary, and chemical mutagens undergo metabolic activation and induce direct or oxidative DNA damage in tissues.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, microenvironmental inflammation, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail non-mutagenic factors that facilitate cancer development, including inflammatory tumor promoters, life-stage vulnerabilities, and an overarching summary of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Methodologies for assessing carcinogenicity and evaluating risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the analytical, experimental, and epidemiological methods used to determine whether exposures cause cancer and how society weighs these risks.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and final summary
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation by summarizing the main takeaways on environmental cancer risks and acknowledging the audience.
